controls.name: Least-privilege identity and short-lived credentials
controls.purpose: Limit agent access to minimum required resources and actions.
controls.implementation: Use agent-specific identities, scoped short-lived credentials, separate read/write scopes, and resource-level authorization on every call.
controls.evidence: Permission matrix, TTL settings, access-denial and revocation tests.

controls.name: Tool allowlist and schema validation
controls.purpose: Constrain tools and reject unsafe or malformed arguments.
controls.implementation: Use server-side tool allowlists, strict schemas, range checks, and business-rule validation; never rely on model-selected arguments alone.
controls.evidence: Tool inventory, schema tests, denied unapproved-tool calls.

controls.name: Human approval for consequential actions
controls.purpose: Prevent unreviewed irreversible or high-impact actions.
controls.implementation: Require authenticated human approval before payments, external messages, HR record changes, deployments or account modifications.
controls.evidence: Approval config, approver identity/timestamps, reject and timeout tests.

controls.name: Trusted-instruction boundary and prompt-injection handling
controls.purpose: Separate trusted instructions from untrusted user, retrieval and tool content.
controls.implementation: Label retrieved content as untrusted; preserve provenance; do not execute instructions inside documents; enforce policies outside the model.
controls.evidence: Indirect-injection tests, provenance labels, traces showing blocked tool actions.

controls.name: Sandboxing and egress restrictions
controls.purpose: Contain code execution and block unauthorised network destinations.
controls.implementation: Use disposable least-privilege sandboxes, restricted filesystem/process/network access, egress allowlists and resource quotas.
controls.evidence: Sandbox settings, blocked egress tests, isolation and resource-limit results.

controls.name: Memory provenance, write controls and retention
controls.purpose: Prevent untrusted or stale content becoming durable memory.
controls.implementation: Record source, author, timestamp and trust; restrict writes; apply TTL, quarantine, review and deletion.
controls.evidence: Memory schema, write authorization tests, provenance and deletion logs.

controls.name: Authenticated inter-agent communication and typed contracts
controls.purpose: Prevent spoofed, replayed or malformed peer messages.
controls.implementation: Authenticate agent identities, validate sender/recipient/purpose, use typed schemas, and limit delegated scope.
controls.evidence: Agent registry, schema contract tests, spoof/replay rejection results.

controls.name: Rate limits, timeouts, budgets and circuit breakers
controls.purpose: Contain retries, runaway loops, cascading failures and cost spikes.
controls.implementation: Set step/tool-call/token/cost budgets, retry ceilings, timeouts, concurrency caps and circuit breakers.
controls.evidence: Quota settings, retry tests, breaker telemetry and cost alerts.

controls.name: Tamper-evident audit logs and end-to-end traces
controls.purpose: Make agent actions, approvals and delegated decisions reconstructable.
controls.implementation: Log principal, model/version, retrieval sources, tool inputs/outputs, policy decisions, approvals and timestamps; protect log integrity.
controls.evidence: End-to-end trace, retention policy, log access controls, reconstruction exercise.

controls.name: Output validation, DLP and privacy filtering
controls.purpose: Prevent unsafe or sensitive model output reaching users or downstream systems.
controls.implementation: Validate output schemas/business rules, redact sensitive data, encode for destination and inspect outbound payloads.
controls.evidence: DLP/redaction tests, schema validation and sensitive-data canaries.

controls.name: Supply-chain verification and dependency governance
controls.purpose: Reduce risk from frameworks, models, tools, plugins and dependencies.
controls.implementation: Pin and verify versions/artifact provenance, scan packages, review permissions, maintain SBOM and test upgrades.
controls.evidence: SBOM, lockfiles, signatures/checksums, scan results and vendor review.

controls.name: Continuous evaluation, red-team tests and incident response
controls.purpose: Verify controls under realistic failure conditions and detect regression.
controls.implementation: Maintain scenario-based evaluations, monitor drift, track remediation and test rollback/kill switch.
controls.evidence: Dated test results, issue remediation, monitoring thresholds, kill-switch exercise.

scenarios.name: Agent Goal Hijack
scenarios.description: Untrusted or adversarial content changes the agent goal or causes it to disregard the intended task boundary.
scenarios.failure_mode: The agent follows hostile instructions embedded in a prompt, email, web page or retrieved document.
recommendations: Separate trusted policy from untrusted content.
Enforce server-side authorization for every action.
Test indirect prompt injection with benign canary documents.

scenarios.name: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
scenarios.description: An agent uses a legitimate tool in an unsafe, unintended or unauthorised way.
scenarios.failure_mode: A model error or manipulated instruction results in an unapproved query, write, message or transaction.
recommendations: Use a small tool allowlist and validate every argument server-side.
Separate read and write permissions.
Require approval for high-impact actions.

scenarios.name: Identity and Privilege Abuse
scenarios.description: An agent misuses, inherits or escalates delegated identity and privileges.
scenarios.failure_mode: The agent accesses resources outside the requesting user's scope or retains credentials too long.
recommendations: Issue agent-specific short-lived scoped credentials.
Enforce user and tenant authorization at each resource boundary.
Test revocation, expiry and cross-tenant denial.

scenarios.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
scenarios.description: Compromised or poorly governed frameworks, plugins, models or dependencies undermine the agent.
scenarios.failure_mode: A dependency or tool update introduces an unsafe capability or exploitable component.
recommendations: Pin and verify versions and artifact provenance.
Review permissions and maintain an SBOM.
Test upgrades before production.

scenarios.name: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
scenarios.description: Agent-driven code or tool execution escapes intended boundaries.
scenarios.failure_mode: Generated code or tool arguments reach a runtime with excessive host, filesystem or network privileges.
recommendations: Use disposable sandboxes with restricted filesystem/network access.
Never expose production secrets or host mounts.
Require review before production deployment.

scenarios.name: Memory and Context Poisoning
scenarios.description: Untrusted or manipulated information contaminates persistent memory or retrieved context.
scenarios.failure_mode: A poisoned memory item or retrieval source changes future agent decisions.
recommendations: Store provenance and trust labels for each memory item.
Restrict writes and apply TTL, quarantine and review.
Test whether poisoned content alters future tasks.

scenarios.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
scenarios.description: Messages between agents are spoofed, replayed, malformed or trusted without checking identity and scope.
scenarios.failure_mode: A downstream agent accepts instructions from an unverified peer or outside its contract.
recommendations: Authenticate agents and validate message sender, recipient and purpose.
Use typed schemas and reject unexpected fields.
Limit delegation depth and permissions.

scenarios.name: Cascading Failures
scenarios.description: A local error, hallucination, retry loop or compromised component propagates across agents or systems.
scenarios.failure_mode: Retries or downstream agents amplify a mistake, causing repeated actions, cost spikes or service disruption.
recommendations: Set strict step, retry, token and cost budgets.
Add timeouts, idempotency checks and circuit breakers.
Stop workflows on repeated anomalies.

scenarios.name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
scenarios.description: Users over-trust persuasive agent output or approve actions without sufficient context.
scenarios.failure_mode: A person accepts an incorrect recommendation or approves a consequential action without understanding it.
recommendations: Show evidence and the exact action before approval.
Separate recommendation from execution and allow rejection.
Train operators and sample approval quality.

scenarios.name: Rogue Agents
scenarios.description: An agent operates outside its intended objective, permissions or operational boundary.
scenarios.failure_mode: A compromised or misconfigured agent continues acting beyond authorised scope.
recommendations: Use independent policy enforcement outside the model.
Implement a tested kill switch and credential revocation.
Monitor behavioural deviations and retain action traces.
